View documentation FAQs Does routing email through WiseStamp affect SPF or DKIM authentication? Server-side WiseStamp integrations route outbound mail through WiseStamp’s infrastructure, so DNS updates are required to preserve authentication. WiseStamp provides an SPF include record to add to the domain’s SPF policy WiseStamp provides a WiseStamp-specific DKIM record for signing relayed mail Client-side integrations (Apple Mail, Chrome Extension) never route mail and require no DNS changes Without these records, relayed mail can fail SPF or DKIM checks at the receiving server. What is the difference between server-side and client-side signature deployment in WiseStamp? Server-side deployment relays outbound mail through WiseStamp’s infrastructure to insert the signature, which is why it requires SPF and DKIM records. Client-side deployment (a browser extension or a mail app’s own signature field) inserts the signature locally and never touches mail flow, so it carries no DNS or authentication requirement. Does WiseStamp work with Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace? Yes. Both are supported through server-side deployment, applying signatures at the mail transport layer. No client install required on any device Signatures apply identically across desktop, mobile, and webmail Deployment covers Outlook, Exchange Online, and Gmail from one admin console What access does WiseStamp need to sync directory data? WiseStamp requests read-only access to directory attributes needed for signature fields and lifecycle events such as hire and departure. Admin consent is required at setup for both Google Workspace Directory and Microsoft Entra ID. WiseStamp does not request write access to the directory itself. Does WiseStamp support single sign-on for admin accounts? Yes. WiseStamp supports SAML 2.0 single sign-on through Okta, Google Workspace, OneLogin, or Microsoft Entra ID. This governs how WiseStamp admins authenticate into the WiseStamp console. Is single sign-on the same as directory sync in WiseStamp? No. Single sign-on controls how admins log into the WiseStamp console. Directory sync controls where employee data comes from and drives automatic signature provisioning. The two are configured independently, and enabling one does not enable the other. Can WiseStamp scope directory sync to specific departments or groups? Yes, for Microsoft Entra ID. Sync can be scoped to specific organizational units, departments, or a named security group, rather than syncing the entire directory. This lets IT stage a rollout to one group before extending it company-wide. What happens to an employee’s signature when they leave the company? For directories with lifecycle automation enabled (Google Workspace Directory, Microsoft Entra ID), WiseStamp deprovisions the signature automatically when the employee’s account is deactivated in the directory. No manual removal step is required. Does WiseStamp integrate with CRM platforms? Yes, through one server-side connection that applies to CRM-sent email regardless of which CRM is in use. Salesforce HubSpot Zoho CRM Pipedrive Marketo Salesloft Microsoft Dynamics 365 NetSuite No separate setup is required per platform. It supports multiple signatures per account and does not route mail through WiseStamp’s servers, so it requires no SPF, DKIM, or mail server changes. Set an auto Gmail signature and insert special features like images and links. Reading time: 4 min Author: Amotz Harari Updated: August 25, 2026 How to add a signature to Gmail (Mac and PC) Gmail does not have a desktop app for both PC and Mac operating systems. The only way to access your account is via the Gmail web version, which works similarly on both systems. Step 1 Open Gmail Settings In the top right corner of your screen, click on the gear icon and then click “See all settings” in the Quick settings panel. Step 2 Navigate to the signature section In the settings panel, scroll down to get to the Signature tab. Click on the “Create New” button to add a Gmail signature. Step 3 Add your signature details Create your signature in the text box to the right of your signature name. Ensure you include your full name, job title, company name, and contact information. Step 4 Edit your Gmail signature The next step is using the rich text editor to make your signature look neat and professional. Here’s how to edit signatures in Gmail: Change font size: Select the signature text you would like to edit Click on the tT icon at the left of the toolbar > choose the text size you’d like to use (Small, Normal, Large, or Huge) Change text color: Click on the A icon at the right of the signature editor’s toolbar Pick the text color you’d like to use from the right-side color pallet Change signature font: Click where it says “Sans serif” on the left side of the editor’s toolbar Choose the font you’d like to use for your signature (these are all email-safe fonts) Step 5 Set auto Gmail signatures and save Just below the signature editor, you’ll see additional settings that let you tell Gmail which signature to set as your auto signature for New and Reply/Forward messages. Lastly, scroll down to the bottom page and click “Save changes.” How to create a signature in Gmail mobile app (Android) The email signature you create on Gmail’s web version is not applied to the emails you send from your phone. The only exception is if you are using a Gmail signature generator, which applies your signatures to all your devices automatically. If you mostly compose emails using your phone, adding a Gmail digital signature becomes necessary. Setting up signatures in Gmail mobile app (Android) Step 1 Launch the Gmail app on your Android phone Step 2 Navigate to Gmail signature settings Click the three-line icon at the top-left corner of your phone’s screen. Scroll down and tap “Settings.” Step 3 Select your email address If you have multiple email addresses attached to your phone, you’ll be prompted to choose the account you wish to make changes to from a list. Step 4 Navigate to mobile signature and design your signature Scroll down to the Mobile signature section. Tap on it and type your signature. Note that the Gmail app version only supports plain text signatures. Click “OK” when you’re done to save your signature. How to add a signature in the Gmail iPhone app (iOS) Gmail signature settings look a little different on Android and iPhone, and the setup steps vary slightly, too. Here’s how to set up a Gmail signature on iPhone: Step 1 Navigate to signature settings on the Gmail app Open the Gmail app on your iPhone and click on the hamburger icon at the top-left corner of the screen. Scroll down and tap on signature settings. Step 2 Type your signature In the window that opens, enable mobile signature. Type your signature in the text box that comes up. Tap Done at the top-right corner of the screen to save your signature. Step 3 Test your signature That’s how to insert a signature in Gmail on an iPhone. Try composing a new email. Your new signature should appear in the body of your email. Navigate to Gmail signature settings > signature defaults and double-check that you have selected the correct signature as your default. Remember to click “Save changes” at the bottom of the page. Images missing in the signature A common reason for images not appearing in email signatures is that they are hosted on a private server. To fix this issue, use a working image URL or upload an image from your device. Keep in mind that your images may not appear if they are too large. Keep image file sizes under 1MB to minimize load times.
